surface: Agent tile, Chatbox compose box (typing into the bottom compose panel while the transcript is above it)
whatRunsAndWhy: Every char typed into the compose box hits handle_claude_key's in_chatbox branch and calls cx.notify() (agent_ui.rs:3379/3381). Because YaldaGpuiView is the only entity, the whole root render() reruns, including render_agent (screens.rs:764). The compose panel lives INSIDE render_agent's pass (screens.rs:~1914-2008), so the static transcript above it is re-walked and re-laid-out: view_model_fingerprint check (agent.rs), reconcile_list (screens.rs:943), reveal_tail_if_following (screens.rs:961), and crucially GPUI re-prepaints/re-lays-out the transcript gpui::list element tree (screens.rs:1489) every keystroke even though the transcript content did not change. The S1 memo, lines_cache, and hl-cache prevent re-derivation of content, but NOT the layout pass over the produced element tree. This is the known flagship open item.
costClass: O(visible-transcript-rows) layout per keystroke (virtualized list still re-lays-out its visible window + measures); plus O(1) fingerprint/reconcile guards
recommendation: Split the transcript into its own child Entity rendered as transcript.into_any().cached(size_full); notify it only when its render fingerprint (view_model_fp + edit_seq + theme + cursor-in-transcript + scroll intent) actually changes. A compose keystroke then dirties only the compose subtree; the transcript's laid-out tree is reused. Keep the compose panel as a separate (small) child so its notify never touches the transcript's dirty set.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: chatbox-keystroke (typing into the Message Box / chatbox compose panel with a bound session and a transcript above)
verdict.correctedCostClass: O(visible-transcript-rows) GPUI layout/prepaint per keystroke (virtualized list re-lays-out only its visible window, not all ~680 items), plus O(1) S1-fingerprint/reconcile/reveal guards and an O(visible) element rebuild inside render_agent. NOT O(all transcript rows).
verdict.reasoning: Confirmed against source. (1) Trigger is real: agent_ui.rs:3349 in_chatbox branch handles every chatbox keystroke and calls cx.notify() at 3379 (paste) / 3381 (default arm). (2) Single-entity model confirmed: only one `impl Render` exists (main.rs:5879 YaldaGpuiView); cx.notify() dirties the root, so the whole tree re-renders — render() cannot be skipped. (3) Transcript is NOT a cached child entity: the only `.cached(` in the render path is `c.view_model.cached(view_model_fp)` (screens.rs:922), which is the S1 *data*-structure memo, not GPUI's AnyView::cached(style) element-tree reuse. grep found no AnyView .cached() anywhere. (4) Compose and transcript share one render pass: render_agent builds the compose_panel (screens.rs:~1921, `InputSurface::Chatbox`) and the transcript `gpui::list(c.list_state.clone(), render_fn).flex_1().w_full()` (screens.rs:1489) in the same function body, so a chatbox keystroke re-runs render_agent and re-emits the transcript list element; GPUI then re-prepaints/re-lays-out its visible window after render returns. (5) Existing guards correctly characterized: view_model.cached (922), reconcile_list (943), reveal_tail_if_following (961) prevent content re-derivation but do NOT skip the layout pass over the produced element tree. One correction to the finding's cost class: the list is virtualized with default visible-only measuring (explicitly NOT ListSizingBehavior::Auto, per the comment + code at 1477-1492), so the per-keystroke layout is O(visible rows), not O(all transcript rows) — the finding already says "virtualized list still re-lays-out its visible window," so this matches. Impact high: it is a constant-interaction surface (typing), it fires every keystroke, the cost is GPUI layout the [perf] flag can't see, and it is the explicitly-named flagship open item. Treatment (split transcript into a cached child Entity, notify only on its render fingerprint) matches the prompt's ground-truth fix.

surface: File-browser tile filter field (Cmd+O picker) and the file-browser rail filter — typing to filter

whatRunsAndWhy: Each filter char calls fb.set_filter -> rebuild_filtered (file_browser.rs:313, O(entries) substring scan) then cx.notify(). render_browser itself is window-capped (builds at most 80 rows, screens.rs:2737), so the file list is bounded. costClass: O(entries) filter scan per keystroke (bounded by one dir) + O(visible) per sibling leaf re-layout
recommendation: Covered by the per-leaf cached-child-Entity treatment: a browser filter keystroke would then only dirty the browser leaf, leaving sibling agent/doc/edit leaves' laid-out trees reused. Optionally debounce/coalesce rebuild_filtered if profiling shows the substring scan matters on large directories.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: browser-filter-keystroke (Key::Char in the Cmd+O picker at browser_ui.rs:267-272 and the rail filter at browser_ui.rs:681-687); both directly call fb.set_filter then cx.notify() with no debounce or seq guard
verdict.correctedCostClass: Per keystroke: blocking RECURSIVE filesystem I/O on the event/paint thread (fs::read_dir + fs::metadata per entry, depth<=MAX_SEARCH_DEPTH=8, capped at MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS=200) via rebuild_filtered->search_recursive, PLUS O(entries) shallow substring scan, PLUS a root cx.notify() that re-lays-out every visible sibling leaf (chrome.rs renders each leaf inline, no .cached()). Net: I/O-bound recursive walk + O(visible-siblings) relayout per keystroke.
verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED REAL and UNGUARDED. browser_ui.rs:267-272 and :681-687 each call fb.set_filter(&text) then cx.notify() directly in the Key::Char handler — no debounce, no fingerprint/seq guard. set_filter (file_browser.rs:195-199) unconditionally calls rebuild_filtered (file_browser.rs:313). The finding MATERIALLY UNDERSTATED the cost: rebuild_filtered is not just an 'O(entries) substring scan over one dir listing' — it also invokes search_recursive (file_browser.rs:331, body 524-573), which performs SYNCHRONOUS RECURSIVE filesystem I/O (fs::read_dir at :536, fs::metadata at :552 per entry) up to MAX_SEARCH_DEPTH=8 / MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS=200 (file_browser.rs:6-7,532) on the event thread, every keystroke. The sibling-relayout claim is also correct: chrome.rs:674-685 renders each leaf's content inline (render_browser/render_doc/render_edit/render_agent -> AnyElement) with NO .cached() wrapper, so the root cx.notify() forces every visible leaf to re-render and re-lay-out — confirming the per-frame cost of the only-one-GPUI-entity model. Two caveats keep this medium not high: (1) the blocking recursive walk is bounded (depth 8, 200 results) and the filter field is used in short bursts, not continuously like the chatbox; (2) the finding's proposed cached-child-entity treatment fixes the sibling relayout but does NOT fix the more serious blocking fs I/O on the paint thread — that needs debouncing/coalescing or moving search_recursive off-thread. Confidence in the finding's existence is high; its cost characterization needed correction upward (blocking I/O) and its treatment is incomplete.

location: src/bin/yalda-gpui/screens.rs:1299-1323 (multi-tool loop 1312; single-tool body 1304) feeding tool_body_free at src/bin/yalda-gpui/agent.rs:359
whatRunsAndWhy: gpui::list virtualizes TOP-LEVEL transcript items, but a single FlatItem::ToolGroup is ONE list item whose interior is built in full when expanded. Two compounding O(data) costs inside that one item: (1) the tool-group merge (agent.rs:2007) coalesces a whole contiguous run of tool calls (e.g. '4 grep, 3 edit, 7 read') into one ToolGroup, and when expanded with count>1 the loop at screens.rs:1312 `for tc in &calls` materializes ALL N tool blocks (build_tool_block_with_weak) as children of that single item; (2) each Full/diff-policy body has max_lines=None, and tool_body_free (agent.rs:359 `for line in display.lines()`) emits ONE div per content line with payloads capped only at TOOL_PAYLOAD_MAX_CHARS=65_536 (agent.rs:821) — so a large expanded edit/diff produces hundreds-to-thousands of per-line div elements. Because the transcript is not a cached child entity, any chatbox compose keystroke notifies the root (agent_ui.rs:3381) and re-lays-out render_agent; if the visible window includes an expanded large group, GPUI re-runs taffy layout + text measurement over that whole un-virtualized interior every keystroke. The S1 view-model memo does NOT help: ToolGroup carries only ids, and tool content is rebuilt inside the closure from tool_calls_snap each render (the fingerprint deliberately excludes it).
costClass: O(expanded-group-content) per keystroke — up to O(tools-in-group × body-lines), body bounded only at 64K chars (~thousands of lines)
recommendation: Split an expanded ToolGroup's interior so it isn't one monolithic list item. Cheapest durable fix: cap rendered body lines for Full/diff policy the same way Truncated does (give the expanded body a hard max_lines with a '+N hidden' footer) so tool_body_free can never emit thousands of divs; and/or promote a large/expanded multi-tool group to its own gpui::list (or flatten each tool block into its own top-level FlatItem so the outer transcript list windows them). Combined with the planned transcript-as-cached-child-entity move, the per-keystroke re-layout of an expanded group disappears entirely.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: chatbox-keystroke (and any cx.notify() / streaming frame) — but only when the visible transcript window actually contains an EXPANDED multi-line ToolGroup
verdict.correctedCostClass: O(visible-expanded-group-body-lines) taffy layout per keystroke. Per-group bounded by TOOL_PAYLOAD_MAX_CHARS=65_536 chars of body => up to ~thousands of per-line divs for a Full/diff policy item; for count>1 groups, summed over every tool in the run. Zero when no expanded group is in the visible window (default = collapsed).
verdict.reasoning: The mechanism is real and unguarded on the cited path. (1) chatbox keystroke -> cx.notify() at agent_ui.rs:3381 dirties the sole root entity, so per the GPUI model the whole tree (including render_agent and its transcript gpui::list) re-renders. (2) The compose panel and the transcript list live in the SAME render_agent body (compose panel appended at screens.rs:1914+; transcript list built earlier), so they re-render together. (3) Decisive evidence in gpui-0.2.2 list.rs:632-657: layout_items calls render_item(item_index) AND element.layout_as_root(...) for EVERY item where visible_height < available_height on every prepaint; the cached item.size() only spares non-visible overdraw items (line 642 still re-renders anything actually visible). So a visible list item is fully re-rendered + re-laid-out each keystroke. (4) For a ToolGroup, the interior is built eagerly inside the list closure: screens.rs:1299-1324 either append_tool_body (single) or `for tc in &calls { ... build_tool_block_with_weak }` (count>1, the merged run from agent.rs:1997-2018). (5) Full policy (Edit/Move/Delete/Think/Other, agent.rs:413-419) passes max_lines=None into tool_body_free, whose loop at agent.rs:359 emits one div per body line, capped only at TOOL_PAYLOAD_MAX_CHARS=65_536 (agent.rs:821). So one expanded large diff = hundreds-to-thousands of divs re-laid-out per keystroke. (6) The S1 view-model memo genuinely does NOT cover this: the comment at screens.rs:909-913 confirms ToolGroup carries only ids and tool content is rebuilt from tool_calls_snap (screens.rs:988) inside the closure, deliberately excluded from view_model_fingerprint. Truncated/HeaderOnly policies are already bounded (truncate_lines at agent.rs:609 adds a '+N hidden' footer), so the gap is specifically the Full/diff policy. Why medium not high: the trigger requires the user to have EXPANDED a large group (default groups render collapsed per agent.rs:2005) AND that group to be in the visible window; in the common collapsed/header-only state the cost is ~zero. When those conditions hold it is genuinely per-keystroke O(n) on the surface the user types in, which is why it's not low. The recommended fix (cap Full-policy expanded bodies with a max_lines like Truncated already does, and/or the planned transcript-as-cached-child-entity move) is sound.

whatRunsAndWhy: When the chatbox draft exceeds COMPOSE_MAX_VISIBLE_LINES (8), every compose keystroke fires cx.notify() (agent_ui.rs:3381) which re-runs render_agent and rebuilds a full `lines_snap: Rc<Vec<String>>` by iterating ALL draft lines and doing a per-line `trim_end_matches('\n').replace('\t', "    ")` — an O(draft) String allocation pass — even though gpui::list only renders the visible 8 rows. There is NO edit_seq guard. The transcript path solves exactly this with `lines_cache`/`lines_cache_seq` (AgentState, screens.rs:840-856), but the Chatbox struct (agent.rs:1456) has no lines_cache/lines_cache_seq field, so the compose draft re-allocates every line every keystroke. For a long pasted draft this is the same class of per-keystroke O(N) String churn the transcript already eliminated.
costClass: O(draft) allocs per chatbox keystroke
recommendation: Add `lines_cache: Rc<Vec<String>>` + `lines_cache_seq: u64` to the Chatbox struct (agent.rs:1456) and gate the long-draft `lines_snap` build on `tb.editor.document().edit_seq()`, reusing the Rc verbatim on cursor-only changes — identical to the AgentState lines_cache idiom. Also `tb.list_state.reset(line_count)` on every keystroke (screens.rs:2006) discards the height cache; prefer splice-on-count-change so unchanged rows keep their measured heights.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: chatbox-keystroke (every compose keystroke when draft > COMPOSE_MAX_VISIBLE_LINES=8 lines): the Claude key handler ends in cx.notify() (agent_ui.rs:3381) which dirties the only GPUI entity (root), so render_agent re-runs and rebuilds lines_snap each frame
verdict.correctedCostClass: O(draft) String allocations per chatbox keystroke (one trim_end_matches + replace('\t') alloc per draft line), unguarded — but only on the long-draft (>8 line) virtualized branch
verdict.reasoning: Verified against source. screens.rs:1996-2005 unconditionally builds `lines_snap: Rc<Vec<String>>` by iterating all `line_count` lines with `doc.line_text(i).trim_end_matches('\n').replace('\t', "    ")` — an O(draft) per-line String alloc. gpui::list virtualizes the ELEMENT build/layout to the visible 8 rows (render_fn at 2011-2029), but the String-extraction pass at 1996-2005 runs over the full draft regardless. The Chatbox struct (agent.rs:1456) holds only editor/mode/scroll_handle/list_state — no lines_cache/lines_cache_seq — so there is genuinely NO seq guard, unlike the transcript path which gates the identical line-extraction on `c.lines_cache_seq == edit_seq` (screens.rs:840-856) and reuses the Rc verbatim. Trigger is confirmed: chatbox key edits route through cx.notify() (agent_ui.rs:3381, and the dedicated chatbox notify at 3380), dirtying the sole root entity → full render_agent every keystroke. The proposed fix is feasible: document().edit_seq() exists (document.rs:106). Downgraded from high to medium because: (1) the cost only applies on the long-draft branch (line_count > 8), so short drafts — the common case — are unaffected; (2) a seq guard (the recommended fix) helps only on NON-mutating keystrokes (arrows, mode toggle, selection) and incidental blink/cross-tile notifies, because on actual character typing edit_seq increments every keystroke, so the O(draft) String pass would still run while typing — the guard does not eliminate the typing-time cost it's framed against; (3) the String-extraction pass is cheaper than the element-build/layout cost already eliminated by virtualization. The secondary list_state.reset(line_count) point (screens.rs:2006) is also real: it discards the height cache every frame. Net: a real, unguarded, on-hot-path per-keystroke O(draft) derivation worth fixing, but bounded and partially mitigated.

whatRunsAndWhy: In the WP edit view, a fresh `kinds: Vec<WpLineKind>` is allocated (with_capacity(line_count)) and `classify_wp_line` is folded over EVERY line of the buffer on every render. Edit-mode keystrokes (edit_ui.rs notify sites) dirty the root, so this O(document) byte-scan + Vec allocation runs per keystroke. The `highlight_snapshot` call immediately above it IS incrementally cached on edit_seq, but the line-kind classification is not — despite being a pure function of the line text (the running fence state is deterministic from edit_seq). The Code edit view has no equivalent per-frame full-buffer pass; this is a WP-only gap.
costClass: O(document) classify + alloc per WP keystroke
recommendation: Cache the `Vec<WpLineKind>` on EditState keyed by edit_seq (same shape as lines_cache/highlight_snapshot) and reuse it when edit_seq is unchanged (cursor moves, cross-tile notifies, selection). Because classify_wp_line carries fence state, recompute the whole vec only on an actual edit; an incremental version that re-folds from the first changed line is a further optimization but the seq guard alone removes the cursor-blink/idle-notify cost.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: WP edit-view render — fires on every root re-render while the active Buffer is in EditView::WordProcessor: edit keystrokes (cx.notify dirties the single root entity), plus cursor moves, selection changes, and any cross-tile/idle notify (no seq guard). Does NOT run in the default Code/RAW edit view.
verdict.correctedCostClass: O(document) per WP-view render: one Vec::with_capacity(line_count) allocation + a per-line byte-scan fold of classify_wp_line. Per-line work is cheap (no allocation, prefix/char checks only); dominant cost is the alloc + loop proportional to line count.
verdict.reasoning: Confirmed real and unguarded. build_edit_body_wp (screens.rs:566) is dispatched directly from render_edit (screens.rs:294) for EditView::WordProcessor, and the kinds vec is freshly allocated + folded over every line each call (screens.rs:585-593) with no edit_seq gate. The contrast the finding draws holds exactly: the highlight_snapshot call one block above (screens.rs:577 -> main.rs:1114-1134) IS cached on edit_seq via lines_cache_seq and highlight_cache.snapshot_syn, while kinds is not — so on cursor-blink/selection/idle notifies (unchanged edit_seq) the highlight path recomputes zero but the classification still re-runs. cx.notify dirties the lone root entity so the whole tree re-renders per keystroke, making this run per-keystroke in WP mode. Treatment (cache Vec<WpLineKind> on EditState keyed by edit_seq, same shape as lines_cache) is correct. Impact is medium, not high: (1) it is conditional on the WordProcessor submode, not the default RAW edit view the user lives in; (2) classify_wp_line (render_blocks.rs:1562) is a trivial allocation-free byte scan, so absolute cost is far below the adjacent syntect highlight pass and far below the known dominant cost (whole-root re-render / transcript re-layout per chatbox keystroke). It is a frequent-but-bounded, guarded-but-improvable allocation, so the seq guard is a cheap correctness-of-pattern win rather than a fix for a user-visible stall.

surface: Edit view + Agent chatbox/worksheet paste (shared dispatch_normal_core / apply_paste)
location: src/bin/yalda-gpui/main.rs:5794 (read_from_clipboard via Command::new("pbpaste").output()); callers: edit_ui.rs:882 (apply_paste), main.rs:2680, agent_ui.rs:3377/3439
whatRunsAndWhy: On a paste keystroke (Cmd-V / `p` / `P` in Normal mode, in the edit view AND the agent chatbox/worksheet via shared apply_paste), the input-thread key handler calls read_from_clipboard(), which runs `Command::new("pbpaste").output()`. `.output()` fork+exec's a subprocess AND BLOCKS the input thread waiting for it to exit before the handler returns and the frame can be scheduled. A subprocess spawn+wait is on the order of 10-50ms of dead time on the paint/input thread per paste — a clipboard read does not need to be synchronous with the keystroke.
costClass: O(1)-but-blocking-subprocess (fork+exec+wait, ~tens of ms)
recommendation: Read the clipboard off the input thread. Prefer GPUI's own clipboard API (cx.read_from_clipboard()) which is in-process and non-blocking instead of shelling out to pbpaste; or, if pbpaste must stay, run it in cx.background_executor().spawn(...) and apply the paste back on the foreground via an async continuation. Do not `.output()`-wait inside the key handler.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: A discrete paste gesture (Cmd-V via PasteFromClipboard action, or vim `p`/`P` producing NormalOutcome::Paste) in the Edit view, Agent chatbox, and Agent worksheet — NOT on every typing keystroke. It runs synchronously on the foreground/paint thread inside the key/action handler.
verdict.correctedCostClass: O(1) but blocking: a synchronous pbpaste subprocess fork+exec+wait (~tens of ms) on the foreground thread, once per paste event. One-frame stall per paste, not per-frame or per-keystroke.
verdict.reasoning: The blocking I/O is real and unguarded. main.rs:5794-5802 read_from_clipboard() runs `Command::new("pbpaste").output()`, which fork+exec's a subprocess and blocks the caller until it exits. apply_paste (edit_ui.rs:881-886) calls it directly, with no async/background-executor wrapping. All four call sites run on the foreground thread inside synchronous key/action handlers: edit_ui.rs:616-623 (Edit view NormalOutcome::Paste), agent_ui.rs:3373-3379 (Agent chatbox) and 3437-3444 (Agent worksheet/editor), and main.rs:2680 (PasteFromClipboard / Cmd-V action). Each is immediately followed by cx.notify(), confirming it is on the same thread that drives Render. No cache or seq guard short-circuits the spawn. So the blocking-IO-on-paint-thread claim holds. The one correction to the finding's framing: the trigger is the discrete paste gesture, not the continuous typing hot path. NormalOutcome::Paste is only emitted by the paste keybinds (edit_ui.rs:732-733), so ordinary typing never hits this — it fires once per paste. That makes it a genuine UI-responsiveness violation (a tens-of-ms hitch on the frame where you paste) but occasional and bounded, so medium rather than high. The recommended fix is sound: use GPUI's in-process clipboard (cx.read_from_clipboard) instead of shelling out, or at minimum spawn pbpaste on the background executor and apply the result via an async continuation; do not .output()-wait in the handler.

surface: Edit view + Agent chatbox/worksheet Normal-mode yank/delete (shared dispatch_normal_core)
location: src/bin/yalda-gpui/main.rs:5786 (yank_to_clipboard via Command::new("pbcopy").spawn()); callers in dispatch_normal_core at edit_ui.rs:780 (yank-selection), 796 (delete-char `x`), 803 (delete-line `dd`), plus 837/842, main.rs:2610/2747/2772
whatRunsAndWhy: `dispatch_normal_core` is the shared Normal-mode dispatcher used by the edit view AND the agent chatbox/worksheet. Several COMMON editing keys route through yank_to_clipboard(): `x` (delete-char, edit_ui.rs:796), `dd` (delete-line, 803), and any yank-selection (780). Each spawns `pbcopy` as a subprocess on the input thread and writes the payload to its stdin synchronously inside the handler. Unlike pbpaste this uses .spawn() (not .output()) so it doesn't wait for exit, but fork+exec of a child process plus the synchronous stdin write_all still executes blocking syscalls on the paint/input thread on every `x`/`dd`/yank — turning ordinary vim-style editing keystrokes into per-keystroke process spawns.
costClass: O(1)-but-blocking-subprocess (fork+exec + synchronous stdin write per keystroke)
recommendation: Use the in-process GPUI clipboard write (cx.write_to_clipboard(...)) instead of spawning pbcopy; failing that, hand the text to cx.background_executor().spawn(...) so the fork+exec+stdin-write happens off the input thread. The handler should only stage the yanked text, not spawn a process.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: Normal-mode yank/delete keys (x / dd / yank-selection / delete-selection / change-selection) in the edit view AND the agent chatbox/worksheet — NOT every keystroke. Insert-mode typing (the dominant chatbox activity) routes through dispatch_insert_core and never calls yank_to_clipboard.
verdict.correctedCostClass: O(1)-per-key blocking syscalls on the input thread: fork+exec of a pbcopy child (spawn, several ms) + synchronous stdin.write_all to the child pipe. NOT blocking-on-exit (.spawn(), no wait/output), but the spawn + pipe write are blocking syscalls. Bounded, not O(n), not per-frame.
verdict.reasoning: Confirmed real and unguarded. yank_to_clipboard at main.rs:5783-5791 does `Command::new("pbcopy").stdin(piped).spawn()` then `stdin.write_all(text)` inline; it is a static fn taking only `&str` (no cx/executor), so there is no possibility of an existing background hop — it executes synchronously on the calling (input) thread. It is reached from the shared dispatcher dispatch_normal_core: edit_ui.rs:780 (yank-selection), 796 (x/delete-char), 803 (dd/delete-line), 837/842 (delete/change-selection). That dispatcher is genuinely shared with the agent surface: agent_ui.rs:3362 (chatbox Normal mode) and 3399 (worksheet Normal mode) both call dispatch_normal_core, so the spawn does run on the agent chatbox/worksheet, validating the cross-surface claim. Two corrections to the finding: (1) Trigger is narrower than 'ordinary editing keystrokes' — it is ONLY Normal-mode yank/delete keys; insert-mode typing (agent_ui.rs:3358/3395 -> dispatch_insert_core) never hits it, and in the chatbox users mostly type in Insert mode, so per-keystroke framing overstates chatbox frequency (though x/dd are common in vim edit-view use). (2) Cost class: the finding's own text already notes .spawn() doesn't wait for exit, so it is NOT a wait-for-subprocess block; the real cost is the fork+exec and the synchronous pipe write, a heavyweight (multi-ms) O(1) operation per key, not O(n) and not per-frame. This is a blocking-IO/responsiveness issue, distinct from the known transcript-re-layout item. The recommended fix is valid and available: gpui 0.2.2 ships cx.write_to_clipboard(ClipboardItem::new_string(...)) (seen in gpui-0.2.2/examples/input.rs:139) and the app does not currently use it (grep for write_to_clipboard/ClipboardItem in src/bin/yalda-gpui returns nothing). Impact medium, not high: real blocking syscalls on user-facing keys and trivially fixable, but bounded O(1), no exit-wait, and the trigger is specific Normal-mode keys rather than per-frame or per-keystroke.

whatRunsAndWhy: Every chatbox keystroke (and paste) calls cx.notify() on the only entity (YaldaGpuiView). That re-runs the entire root render() -> render_focused_window -> render_layout -> render_agent for the focused agent leaf. render_agent rebuilds the full strip/status row, re-evaluates the view-model fingerprint, re-runs reconcile_list, re-takes all the per-frame snapshots (screens.rs:976-1007), and re-prepaints the visible transcript rows via gpui::list — none of which the chatbox draft changed. The transcript content is unchanged, so this is wasted layout/prepaint of an unrelated subtree triggered by typing in a sibling panel. (This is the known open item; confirming it is real and locating the exact notify sites + the wasted render_agent body.)
costClass: O(visible-transcript-rows)+O(strip)+O(snapshots) per keystroke (NOT O(full transcript) — transcript list height cache survives because its edit_seq/count are unchanged, so reconcile_list is a no-op at agent.rs:2608)
recommendation: Split the compose/chatbox panel (screens.rs:1914-2071) into its own child Entity rendered as child.into_any().cached(size_full); have the chatbox key handler notify ONLY that child entity (gated on a compose render fingerprint: draft text seq + cursor line/col + mode + selection). The transcript subtree then keeps its prepaint/paint via cached() because its entity-id stays out of dirty_views, and the root re-render becomes cheap. This converts a per-keystroke transcript re-prepaint into zero transcript work.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: chatbox-keystroke (and paste) — confirmed at agent_ui.rs:3379 (Paste) and :3381 (default arm); both call cx.notify() inside the `if in_chatbox` block (agent_ui.rs:3349)
verdict.correctedCostClass: O(visible-transcript-rows prepaint) + O(strip/status-row element assembly) + O(frozen-ranges) per keystroke. The strip likewise could become a small cached child keyed on a status fingerprint (mode label + cursor L:C + awaiting + status msg + model/perm badge) so it only re-lays-out when those change, not on every transcript keystroke.

whatRunsAndWhy: Every character typed into the filter (browser_ui.rs:270 Char, :260 Backspace, and the rail variant :674/:684) calls b.fb.set_filter(text), which synchronously calls rebuild_filtered -> search_recursive: a BLOCKING recursive filesystem walk (fs::read_dir + an fs::metadata syscall PER entry) from current_dir down to MAX_SEARCH_DEPTH=8, plus a sort, on the UI/paint thread. There is no debounce/coalescing: each keystroke re-walks the tree from scratch. For a rare or non-matching query it walks the ENTIRE subtree to depth 8 (it only short-circuits once it accumulates MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS=200 matches), so a large repo => hundreds-to-thousands of syscalls per keystroke, blocking the frame. This is the single worst input-coalescing offender: filesystem I/O on the keystroke hot path with no debounce and no off-thread execution.
costClass: O(filesystem subtree to depth 8) blocking I/O per keystroke
recommendation: Two stacking fixes: (1) coalesce/debounce — only kick a search after a short idle (e.g. 80-120ms via a cancellable spawned task keyed on filter_text), so a burst of keystrokes runs the walk once, not N times; (2) move-io-off-thread — run search_recursive on cx.background_executor() and apply results via a notify when done, so the paint thread never blocks on fs::read_dir/fs::metadata. A cheap incremental win: when the new query extends the previous one (old is a prefix), filter the prior search_results in memory instead of re-walking the disk.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: browser-filter-keystroke (every Char/Backspace while filter_mode is active in the Cmd+O picker or its rail variant)
verdict.correctedCostClass: O(filesystem subtree to depth 8) blocking I/O per keystroke (fs::read_dir + one fs::metadata syscall per entry, recursing to MAX_SEARCH_DEPTH=8, short-circuiting only at MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS=200 matches), plus a full root re-render via cx.notify()

Then a sort (line 341). All four cited call sites fire per keystroke: picker Backspace browser_ui.rs:260 and Char :270, rail Backspace :674 and Char :684, each followed by cx.notify(). grep confirms NO debounce, NO background_executor, NO spawn anywhere in src/file_browser.rs or browser_ui.rs — the walk runs on the UI/paint thread. The 'already-done' perf work (transcript virtualization, S1 fingerprint, highlight cache) is unrelated and does not touch this path. The handler is gated on filter_mode (browser_ui.rs:214-225), so it only fires while actively typing a filter in the Cmd+O picker — a real but intermittent surface, not a constant-interaction hot path like the message box. That, plus the prefix-extend incremental opportunity the finding itself notes, lands this at medium rather than high: severe per-stroke blocking cost, narrower trigger. The cx.notify() also re-lays-out the whole root each stroke, but the dominant cost is the blocking fs walk. Recommendation (debounce + background_executor, or in-memory prefix filtering when the new query extends the old) is sound.

location: src/bin/yalda-gpui/chrome.rs:542 (desktop_pointer_move); resize notify at :555, drag notify at :601; bound at chrome.rs:155-157
whatRunsAndWhy: During a live tile drag or edge-resize, the canvas on_mouse_move fires desktop_pointer_move on every pointer move tick, which calls cx.notify() unconditionally (resize: :555 on every sub-pixel pointer update; drag: :601 on every move once active) without first checking whether the rendered output actually changed. The resize render only changes at slot-pitch (Block-clamped span) boundaries and the drag render only changes when the target slot or pan changes, yet both notify every pixel. Each notify dirties the single root entity, re-running the full render including render_layout, which re-dispatches every visible leaf to render_doc/render_edit/render_agent. If any tile on that desktop holds an agent, its un-cached transcript subtree re-lays-out on every drag/resize pixel — many redundant full re-layouts for one logical gesture.
costClass: O(visible-split incl. transcript re-layout) per mouse-move tick
recommendation: Gate the notify on a real change: for resize, compute desktop_resize_target_span (already cheap arithmetic) and only notify when the clamped span differs from last frame; for drag, only notify when target slot or pan actually changed (compare against previous d.target / pan before notifying). This collapses a pixel-stream of notifies into one-per-visible-state-change, the same pattern doc_mouse_move already uses (main.rs:2575 only notifies when sel.head != pos).

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: Live desktop-mode tile drag or edge-resize: every OS mouse-move tick while a drag/resize is armed (the on_mouse_move at chrome.rs:155-157 fires per move, but desktop_pointer_move early-returns at :564-566 when no drag AND no resize, so the unconditional cx.notify() only runs during an active gesture). NOT per-keystroke and not on idle hover.
verdict.correctedCostClass: Per mouse-move tick during an active gesture: cx.notify() dirties the single root, re-running render -> render_desktop, which iterates EVERY tile in desktop.slots (chrome.rs:127-132) and re-renders each leaf incl. render_agent (chrome.rs:299-310). NOT a full transcript rebuild: the transcript is virtualized via gpui::list (visible rows only) and the S1 view-model is memoized on view_model_fp (fingerprint hit = no rebuild). So real cost = re-layout of all on-screen desktop tiles' VISIBLE content per pixel. Resize notifies (:555) are mostly redundant (preview is span-clamped via slot_at floor / clamp_span at workspace.rs:915, desktop_resize_target_span chrome.rs:537 -> changes only at slot-pitch). Drag notifies (:601) mostly are NOT redundant: the dragged tile content rides along at d.pointer (chrome.rs:254-257), so output genuinely changes every pixel.
verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED REAL & UNGUARDED for the notify itself: desktop_pointer_move calls cx.notify() with no change-comparison on both paths (chrome.rs:555 resize, :601 drag), unlike the sibling doc_mouse_move which gates on sel.head != pos (main.rs:2575-2580). Trigger verified: on_mouse_move is always armed (chrome.rs:155) but the function returns before notify when neither resize nor drag is set (:551 resize-branch, :564-566 drag guard), so notify only fires during an active gesture, not on idle hover. The re-render does reach un-cached agent transcripts: render_desktop loops all slots (chrome.rs:127) and calls render_agent per tile (:309) with no .cached() wrapper (matches the known-open item that the transcript is not a cached child entity). BUT two things downgrade the finding from the claimed 'high / full transcript re-layout': (1) the transcript list is virtualized and the S1 view-model is fingerprint-memoized, so each notify re-lays-out only VISIBLE rows, not the whole transcript; (2) the trigger is a deliberate, intermittent drag/resize gesture, not a constant per-keystroke/per-scroll interaction. The finding's RESIZE recommendation is correct and sound (span-clamped preview changes only at slot pitch via slot_at floor at workspace.rs:915 / desktop_resize_target_span at chrome.rs:537, so per-pixel resize notifies are genuinely redundant -- gate on clamped-span delta). The finding's DRAG recommendation ('only notify when target slot or pan changed') is WRONG: the dragged tile content rides along continuously at d.pointer (chrome.rs:254-257), so gating on slot/pan would make the ghost jump in slot-sized steps and lose smooth cursor-follow -- drag legitimately needs per-pixel notify. Net: real, partially fixable (resize), bounded by existing virtualization/memoization; medium impact because during the gesture it is per-pixel O(visible desktop tiles incl. their visible transcript rows), which can cause drag/resize jank on a busy desktop, but it is not a constantly-hit hot path.

surface: Rename overlay, Tag-input overlay, and Buffer-switcher filter field — typing into any of these while an Agent tile is the focused leaf behind the dimmed overlay
location: src/bin/yalda-gpui/main.rs:5066-5071 (rename Char), :5090-5095 (tag-input Char), :5302-5304 (buffer-switcher filter Char); underlying screen built unconditionally at main.rs:5952-5953 render_focused_window

So each character typed into the rename/tag/buffer-switcher text field calls cx.notify() and re-runs render_agent for the focused agent tile sitting behind the dimmed overlay, re-laying-out its transcript (screens.rs:764/1489) even though nothing in the transcript changed and it is fully occluded by the overlay. The overlay itself is tiny; the wasted work is the un-cached transcript behind it.
costClass: O(visible-transcript-rows) layout per overlay keystroke, entirely wasted (occluded, unchanged)
recommendation: Same transcript-as-cached-child-Entity fix covers this: once the transcript is a cached child gated on its own fingerprint, an overlay keystroke notifies the root but the transcript's entity-id is not in dirty_views, so its prepaint/paint is reused and only the overlay re-lays-out. (Alternatively, when has_overlay, render_focused_window could reuse a cached snapshot of the underlying screen — but the cached-child-Entity approach is the durable one per the framework model.)

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: edit-keystroke into the rename / tag-input / buffer-switcher overlay text field while an Agent tile is the focused leaf behind the overlay
verdict.correctedCostClass: O(visible-transcript-rows) prepaint/layout per overlay keystroke (NOT O(all rows) — transcript is virtualized; and NOT the flat-item rebuild — that is fingerprint-cached). Wasted because the transcript is occluded and unchanged.
verdict.reasoning:
Mechanism confirmed end-to-end. (1) The overlay Char handlers call cx.notify(): rename main.rs:5070, tag-input main.rs:5094, and the buffer-switcher filter handler — each notify dirties the single root entity (the only impl Render). (2) Root render builds screen_view UNCONDITIONALLY via render_focused_window at main.rs:5953; has_overlay only toggles focus attachment (main.rs:5947-5948 leaf_attach_focus / rail_focused), it does NOT gate whether the underlying screen is built. (3) The built screen_view is then composited as a .child() UNDER each overlay (rename main.rs:6072, buffer-switcher main.rs:6088, session main.rs:6105), so the focused agent leaf's tree is constructed and prepainted every overlay keystroke. (4) For an agent leaf, render_focused_window -> render_agent (screens.rs:764) builds gpui::list(c.list_state.clone(), render_fn) at screens.rs:1489. Per the framework ground truth there is no cached-child-entity, so the list's visible rows are re-laid-out every frame — unguarded by any per-frame skip.

What IS already guarded (so the finding overstates only if read as O(all rows) or as a rebuild): the S1 view-model is fingerprint-memoized (view_model_fingerprint, screens.rs:914-932) — on an overlay keystroke the transcript fingerprint is unchanged, so cached() hits and the expensive flat-item/gutter/tool-anchor rebuild is SKIPPED. And the transcript is virtualized via gpui::list, so only VISIBLE rows are measured, not all. The finding's own costClass already says O(visible-transcript-rows), which matches.

So the residual wasted work is real and unguarded, but it is bounded (visible rows, ~tens) and fires only on a rare, transient interaction (opening an overlay and typing into a single-line field), not the constant chatbox typing that is the KNOWN open item. The recommended fix (transcript as a cached child Entity gated on its fingerprint) is exactly the already-queued chatbox fix and would cover this case for free — i.e. this is a low-impact secondary instance of the known root cause, not a new high-impact hot path. Hence isReal=true, impact=low.

surface: Agent tile, Worksheet mode (the transcript IS the editor; typing a char into it)
whatRunsAndWhy: In Worksheet mode the transcript is the edit target, so re-laying it out on a keystroke is partly legitimate. But the SAME render_agent pass also rebuilds the compose-mode-irrelevant neighbors that did not change: the footer/status strip (screens.rs:1532+), mode label, thinking/elapsed indicator, and (because render_layout walks the whole split, chrome.rs:674-685) any SIBLING leaf in the same split — a sibling agent transcript, doc, or edit pane — all re-lay-out. The transcript edit itself re-runs the full extract/hl/view-model pipeline gated by edit_seq (which DID bump), so that part is expected; the wasted part is sibling leaves + chrome that share the root notify.
costClass: O(visible) for the edited transcript (expected) + O(visible) for each unrelated sibling leaf + footer (wasteful)
recommendation: Make each split LEAF a cached child Entity gated on its own fingerprint, so a worksheet keystroke in leaf A does not re-lay-out sibling leaf B. Separately, split the agent footer/status strip into a cached child so the per-keystroke notify only re-lays-out the transcript body that actually changed, not the status chrome.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: worksheet-keystroke (NormalOutcome::Handled/Yanked/Paste at agent_ui.rs:3428/3433/3443 -> cx.notify() dirties the root -> render_layout walks every leaf, chrome.rs:660-685)

No unguarded O(transcript)-per-sibling cost.
verdict.reasoning: The structural mechanism is real: NormalOutcome::Handled/Yanked/Paste each call cx.notify() (agent_ui.rs:3428/3433/3443), which dirties the single root entity; render_layout (chrome.rs:660-685) then re-renders EVERY split leaf via render_doc/render_edit/render_agent. So sibling leaves and the footer DO get re-rendered on a worksheet keystroke. BUT the finding's cost claim ('O(visible) wasteful per sibling leaf') overstates the marginal cost, because every leaf body is already virtualized and cache-gated: render_doc renders its body through gpui::list with default visible-only measuring (screens.rs:135), skipping its list reset when count is unchanged (screens.rs:42) and doing only cheap Rc/SharedString/Copy clones — its heavy derivation is behind blocks_seq; render_edit is identical (screens.rs:553/731); the agent transcript is gpui::list at screens.rs:1489 with default measuring (the comment at 1478-1488 documents that this is exactly the fix for the per-keystroke O(transcript) layout cost). A sibling whose data didn't change re-runs no O(n) pipeline: lines_cache is gated on edit_seq (screens.rs:840), highlight is incremental (866), and the S1 view-model is fingerprinted (914) — all hit for an untouched sibling. The footer/status strip (screens.rs:1520-1559) is a handful of div().child(format!()) calls, O(1). So the real wasted work per keystroke is small element-tree reassembly + visible-row layout for unchanged siblings/footer, not the implied O(n)-per-sibling. The recommended cached-child-entity treatment is legitimately correct and would eliminate even that residual reassembly + visible-row relayout of unchanged siblings, but because virtualization already caps the cost at O(visible) per surface and siblings are typically few, the impact is low/bounded, not the high per-keystroke O(n) the finding's framing suggests. This is consistent with the orchestrator's KNOWN-open note that the chatbox keystroke still re-renders the whole root — acknowledged, with the heavy work already neutralized.

recommendation: If session counts can grow, apply the same scroll_to_keep_visible skip/take window the file browser and rails already use, or move to gpui::list. Low priority while counts stay small.

whatRunsAndWhy: The WordProcessor edit view runs a full O(line_count) byte-scan classify_wp_line over EVERY line each render to build the `kinds` vector, because classify_wp_line carries running fence state and must be folded in order; the virtualized list closure then indexes it. This is a CPU loop, not element materialization (the row elements themselves ARE virtualized via gpui::list at screens.rs:731), and the in-code comment argues it is cheaper than the per-row element layout the list now skips. It is O(document) per keystroke rather than O(visible), so on a very large buffer it is a per-keystroke linear cost — but it is a cheap byte scan with no allocation per row, so impact is modest. Reported for verification, not as a clear hot-path regression.
costClass: O(document) cheap byte-scan per keystroke
recommendation: If WP typing lag appears on large buffers, make `kinds` incremental like the highlight cache (re-classify only from the first changed line forward, reusing fence state up to the edit point) instead of re-folding the whole document every keystroke. Otherwise leave as-is.

verdict.correctedCostClass: O(document) per frame: full per-line byte/char scan via classify_wp_line + one Vec<WpLineKind> heap allocation of line_count entries. Unguarded by any seq check.
verdict.reasoning: The kinds-precompute loop at screens.rs:585-593 is genuinely unguarded and runs on every call to build_edit_body_wp. That function is invoked from the render path (screens.rs:294), and per the GPUI model cx.notify() dirties the root so every WP edit-view keystroke re-renders the root and re-runs this loop. Critically, the loop has NO seq guard: while the adjacent highlight_snapshot (main.rs:1104-1136) IS cached (lines_cache_seq==edit_seq short-circuits the String rebuild, and snapshot_syn is incrementally cached), the kinds Vec is rebuilt from scratch every frame — Vec::with_capacity(line_count) at screens.rs:585 is one O(document) allocation per frame plus a full ordered fold (fence state forces in-order, so it cannot be windowed without carrying fence state to the edit point). classify_wp_line (render_blocks.rs:1562-1618) is confirmed a cheap char/byte scan returning an enum with NO per-line heap allocation, so the per-row cost is tiny. So the finding is accurate on every structural claim; it only understates one thing — the per-frame Vec allocation (it says 'no allocation', true per-row but there is one O(document) Vec alloc per frame). Impact is low, not high: (a) work per line is trivial; (b) the surface is the narrow WP edit sub-view, not the constantly-used chatbox where the known typing-lag culprit lives (transcript not a cached child entity); (c) the dominant per-row element-layout cost is already virtualized via gpui::list (screens.rs:731). It would only become noticeable on a very large WP buffer, exactly as the finding's own low-confidence framing states. The recommendation to make kinds incremental like the highlight cache is valid but conditional — leave as-is unless WP typing lag is observed on large buffers.

whatRunsAndWhy: `let proc_cwd = process_cwd();` runs unconditionally in the agent status strip on every render_agent call. process_cwd() (persist.rs:39) calls `std::env::current_dir()`, which is a getcwd(2) syscall, executed on the GPUI paint thread once per visible agent tile per frame — i.e. on every chatbox/worksheet keystroke and every streaming notify. The process cwd does not change during a session, so this is a pure per-frame syscall purely to compare against `active_slot_cwd`. Cheap individually but it is blocking-I/O-on-paint-thread that recurs at keystroke frequency and is trivially avoidable.
costClass: O(1) syscall per agent-frame
recommendation: Compute the process cwd once (OnceLock/static, mirroring perf_enabled/hl_cache_enabled in main.rs:130) or cache it on the view at startup, and compare against the cached value instead of calling current_dir() every frame.

verdict.correctedCostClass: O(1) getcwd(2) syscall + one PathBuf alloc per visible agent tile per frame
verdict.reasoning: Confirmed real and unguarded. screens.rs:1603 `let proc_cwd = process_cwd();` sits in the unconditional body of `render_agent` (fn starts screens.rs:764). The status strip is built unconditionally — `let mut strip = div()...` at screens.rs:1508 with line 1603 in the same flat `strip = strip.child(...)` sequence, no enclosing collapse/hidden gate. `render_agent` is invoked from the root render path: chrome.rs:309 and chrome.rs:684 (`App::Agent(tile) => self.render_agent(...)`), called for every visible agent leaf. Per the GPUI model, cx.notify() dirties the sole root entity (YaldaGpuiView) and Window::draw re-renders + re-prepaints the whole tree every frame, so this executes on every chatbox keystroke and every streaming notify, once per visible agent tile. process_cwd() at persist.rs:39-41 is `std::env::current_dir().unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from(\"/\"))` = a real getcwd(2) syscall plus a PathBuf allocation, then `active_slot_cwd != proc_cwd` (screens.rs:1604). No memoization: grep shows NO OnceLock/static or view-field cache for this call — it does NOT mirror the existing `perf_enabled()`/`hl_cache_enabled()` OnceLock guards at main.rs:130/139. The other `proc_cwd` sites (main.rs:1813, agent_ui.rs:44/723/778/1002/1504) are startup/event-handler paths, not per-frame. The recommended fix (OnceLock static or view-field snapshot, since process cwd is invariant within a session) is correct and trivial. Impact downgraded from the finding's 'high' confidence to LOW severity: it is genuinely blocking I/O on the paint thread at keystroke frequency, but a single uncontended getcwd is microsecond-scale and O(1) — not O(n) in user data and not a plausible jank source on its own. It's a worth-fixing correctness-of-discipline nit (no syscalls in render), not a latency driver. The dominant known cost on this trigger remains the un-cached transcript re-layout.

whatRunsAndWhy: `frozen_ranges = c.editor.frozen_lines().to_vec()` (line 898) and `frozen_lines_snap = c.editor.frozen_lines().to_vec()` (line 990) both clone the same `&[(usize,usize)]` slice into a fresh Vec on every render_agent frame, outside the S1 memo boundary. frozen_lines() returns a borrowed slice, so the second copy is redundant — one owned Vec (or passing the slice/an Rc) would serve both the fingerprint/rebuild inputs and the render closure. Allocation is small (one Vec of frozen ranges) but it is unguarded per-frame churn at keystroke frequency, and the second to_vec is pure duplication.
costClass: O(frozen-ranges) alloc x2 per agent-frame
recommendation: Build the frozen-ranges Vec once near line 898 and move/clone-Rc it into the closure at 990 instead of calling frozen_lines().to_vec() a second time; better, keep it as an Rc on AgentState refreshed only when edit_seq changes so the per-frame alloc disappears entirely.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: root render (per-frame); on an agent tile this fires per chatbox-keystroke since the chatbox keystroke re-renders the whole root and render_agent runs unconditionally past the picker early-return
verdict.correctedCostClass: 2x O(frozen-ranges) small Vec alloc per agent render frame; frozen-ranges is a coalesced list of (start,end) pairs (a handful, not per-line), so each Vec is tiny
verdict.reasoning: Both calls verified as real and unguarded. editor.rs:352 `frozen_lines()` returns a borrowed `&[(usize,usize)]` slice, so both `.to_vec()` calls genuinely heap-allocate. screens.rs:898 `let frozen_ranges: Vec<(usize,usize)> = c.editor.frozen_lines().to_vec();` runs before the S1 memo boundary (the `c.view_model.cached(view_model_fp)` check at line 922), and screens.rs:990 `let frozen_lines_snap: Vec<(usize,usize)> = c.editor.frozen_lines().to_vec();` runs after it in the closure-snapshot section — neither is inside the memoized rebuild, so both execute every render_agent frame regardless of the S1 cache hit. render_agent is reached from the single root `impl Render` (YaldaGpuiView) and runs unconditionally once past the picker early-returns at screens.rs:774/779; per the environment's own statement, a chatbox keystroke dirties the root and re-renders the whole tree, so on a visible agent tile both allocs fire per keystroke. The redundancy claim also holds: `frozen_ranges` (898) is only consumed by-reference afterward (line 899 `.iter()`, line 927 `&frozen_ranges`), so it remains owned and in scope at 990 and could simply be moved into the render closure, eliminating the second `.to_vec()`. So the finding is accurate as stated. Impact is LOW, not medium: frozen_lines is a coalesced list of contiguous (start,end) ranges (a handful of frozen turns), NOT one entry per line — the corrected cost is O(frozen-ranges) ~= a few elements, two tiny Vec allocations. They sit on the same frame already doing far heavier unguarded work (the highlight Rc snapshot, view_model_fingerprint, reconcile_list, and several owned snapshots like theme.clone()/calls_snapshot()/expanded_snapshot()). Removing the duplicate is a trivially correct micro-cleanup but will not move the typing-lag needle; the real fix remains making the transcript a cached child entity so the root keystroke stops re-laying-out the transcript at all.

whatRunsAndWhy: save_workspace_state() runs std::env::current_dir() (a getcwd syscall), gc_buffers(), serializes the whole workspace, and synchronously std::fs::writes workspace.json on the input thread. It is called from ~80 sites. Verified that these are STRUCTURAL/lifecycle events (open file, tab/split create/close/focus, mark/tag ops, wiki-link open, reload) and NOT per-keystroke — the per-keystroke insert path (dispatch_insert) does not call it, and disk save_buffer is Ctrl-S only. So this is correct today, but it is a synchronous serialize+fs::write on the input thread that will become a visible hitch if a future caller is added to a hot path, and even now adds a small blocking write to every tab/split/focus action.
costClass: O(workspace)-serialize + blocking fs::write on each structural action
recommendation: Lower priority (not on a per-keystroke path). Consider debouncing/coalescing workspace persistence onto a background task (collect the snapshot on the foreground, serialize+write off-thread) so structural actions never block on disk, and to guard against a future hot-path caller. Flag for verification that no per-keystroke caller exists.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: Structural/lifecycle actions only (open/close file, tab/split create/close, focus change, layout-mode cycle, desktop drag-start commit, workspace move, mark/tag/reload) — ~75 call sites. NOT per-keystroke and NOT per-frame.
verdict.correctedCostClass: Synchronous blocking I/O per structural action: getcwd syscall + gc_buffers sweep + full read-modify-write of the multi-cwd workspace.json (std::fs::read + serde parse + serde_json::to_vec_pretty of whole workspace snapshot + std::fs::write) on the input thread. O(workspace) serialize, not O(keystroke).
verdict.reasoning: The work executes exactly as claimed and is genuinely synchronous blocking I/O on the input/foreground thread. save_workspace_state (main.rs:1684-1692) calls gc_buffers(), std::env::current_dir() (getcwd), then save_persisted_workspace (persist.rs:748-773) which does a read-modify-write: std::fs::read(path) + serde_json::from_slice + snapshot_workspace + serde_json::to_value/to_vec_pretty + std::fs::write — all blocking, no off-thread task, no debounce. So the I/O is real and unguarded by any async path. HOWEVER the trigger is confirmed to be structural/lifecycle only, never a hot path: (1) the per-keystroke edit insert path dispatch_insert (edit_ui.rs:503-517) only calls cx.notify(), no save; (2) the chatbox/compose keystroke path in agent_ui.rs has ZERO calls to save_workspace_state across the whole file — handle_claude_key (agent_ui.rs:3266) routes typing through dispatch_insert_core (lines 3359/3396) with no persist; (3) sampled call sites are all discrete user actions: tab/split create-replace (main.rs:2130), layout-mode cycle (main.rs:3194), workspace move (main.rs:4383), and desktop drag-START mouse-down (chrome.rs:481-489, fired once per drag not per move-frame). Because these are discrete, user-paced events (not held-key repeat or per-frame), a sub-ms-to-low-single-digit-ms blocking write of a ~tens-of-KB JSON file is not perceptible today — hence low impact. The finding itself self-rates lower-priority and flags the verification that no per-keystroke caller exists; that verification passes. The recommendation (coalesce/move serialize+write off-thread) is a reasonable defensive hardening against a future hot-path caller, but is not a current responsiveness defect.

whatRunsAndWhy: While a turn is awaiting, the pump cx.notify()s the root ~1Hz (server pump, gated on awaiting_anim_fingerprint whole-second clock at agent_ui.rs:1418-1421) or every 120ms unconditionally on the legacy direct-spawn path (agent_ui.rs:1213-1219, gated only on any_agent_awaiting, NOT on a fingerprint). Each tick dirties the single entity and re-runs the whole root render() including render_agent, purely to advance a one-line 'Thinking… mm:ss' label and the pulsing dot (screens.rs:1383-1439) at the transcript tail. The direct-spawn path is 8x more frequent than needed because it lacks the second-fingerprint gate the server path has.
costClass: O(visible-transcript-rows)+O(strip) per tick (server: ~1Hz; direct-spawn: ~8Hz)
recommendation: Two parts: (1) Bring the direct-spawn pump (agent_ui.rs:1213-1219) up to parity with the server pump by gating its notify on awaiting_anim_fingerprint() so it fires ~1Hz, not every 120ms. (2) For the durable fix, render the thinking indicator / status-clock as its own tiny child Entity (not a FlatItem in the transcript list) and notify ONLY it on the anim tick; the cached transcript and cached compose then stay out of dirty_views, so the clock tick re-lays-out only the indicator. Note: the sub-second sine pulse at screens.rs:1387 is already effectively frozen between 1Hz notifies — moving it to its own entity is also where you'd add a smooth animation if wanted, without paying transcript cost.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: Timer while a turn is awaiting only (turn_phase.is_awaiting()). Live default path (session-server, start_server_pump) fires at ~1Hz, already gated on awaiting_anim_fingerprint(). The unconditional-120ms (~8Hz) behavior the finding flags is real ONLY on the legacy/fallback direct-spawn pump (start_session_pump), reachable solely when session_server.is_none() (YALDA_SESSION_SERVER=0 or connect failure). Does NOT fire on chatbox keystroke.
verdict.correctedCostClass: Per tick: one cx.notify() dirties the single root entity -> full root render() incl. render_agent. But the transcript is virtualized (gpui::list, measures only visible rows) and the S1 view-model is fingerprint-memoized (no rebuild on a sub-second tick). So real cost is O(visible-transcript-rows re-render) + O(strip), NOT O(full transcript). Frequency: ~1Hz on the live server path; ~8Hz only on the legacy direct-spawn fallback.
verdict.reasoning: Code confirms both claims literally. agent_ui.rs:1213-1219 (direct-spawn pump) notifies every anim_period=120ms (set at :1172) gated only on any_agent_awaiting() (:2856-2860), with NO whole-second fingerprint -> ~8Hz. agent_ui.rs:1410-1426 (server pump) notifies only when awaiting_anim_fingerprint() (:2868-2890, second-granular elapsed+quiet) changes -> ~1Hz, with the comment at :1413-1417 stating exactly this rationale. BUT impact is low for three reasons: (1) The 8Hz path is LEGACY/fallback only -- open_agent_inner at agent_ui.rs:46-62 routes to start_server_pump when session_server.is_some(), and the direct-spawn branch is explicitly labeled 'Direct-spawn path (legacy)' (:62); session_server is Some by default (persist.rs:104-124, only None on YALDA_SESSION_SERVER=0 or connect failure). The live surface already runs the 1Hz fingerprint-gated path. (2) The trigger is a per-second timer that only fires while a turn is awaiting -- it is NOT per-keystroke and NOT per-frame on the user-interactive path; an idle/typing user with no in-flight turn pays nothing. (3) The notify does dirty the root, but the transcript list is virtualized (gpui::list measures visible rows only) and the S1 view-model is fingerprint-memoized, so a sub-second tick rebuilds no view-model and re-lays-out only visible rows + strip, not the whole transcript -- the finding's costClass 'O(visible-transcript-rows)' is right but the recommendation overstates it as 'the dominant idle-stall cost' for the live path, which the existing server-path fingerprint gate already neutralizes. Net: recommendation (1) bringing the legacy pump to fingerprint parity is correct and cheap but affects only the fallback path; recommendation (2) splitting the indicator into a cached child entity is architecturally sound but a 1Hz, virtualization-bounded trigger makes it low priority versus the known open item (chatbox keystroke re-laying out the non-cached transcript).

whatRunsAndWhy: frozen_lines_snap = c.editor.frozen_lines().to_vec() allocates a fresh Vec<(usize,usize)> on EVERY render_agent call (every chatbox keystroke, every worksheet keystroke, every ~1Hz thinking tick, every ACP stream batch). Unlike the adjacent tool_calls_snap/expanded_snap (gen-gated O(1) pointer clones at agent.rs:106-123) and lines_snap/flat_items (Rc clones), this one is an unconditional deep copy. The range vector grows with the number of frozen Claude turn blocks (O(turns)), so it is small early but scales with conversation length and is re-copied on the hot keystroke path for no reason — frozen_lines only changes when a turn finalizes.
costClass: O(frozen-turn-ranges) alloc per render, on every keystroke/tick
recommendation: Give frozen_lines the same gen-gated Rc snapshot treatment as calls_snapshot: cache an Rc<Vec<(usize,usize)>> invalidated only when the frozen set changes (e.g. on turn finalize / a frozen-gen counter), and clone the Rc per render instead of .to_vec(). Removes a per-keystroke allocation that grows with session length.

verdict.actuallyRunsOn: chatbox keystroke (and every other render_agent trigger: worksheet keystroke, ~1Hz thinking tick, ACP stream batch) — the root re-renders on every cx.notify() and render_agent is called from the root render path in chrome.rs:309/684
verdict.correctedCostClass: O(frozen-turn-ranges) per render: one small heap allocation + memcpy of N plain (usize,usize) Copy tuples (16 bytes each), N = count of disjoint frozen blocks. Grows ~linearly with conversation length but with a tiny constant; no string/nested clones.
verdict.reasoning: The finding is accurate. screens.rs:990 `let frozen_lines_snap: Vec<(usize, usize)> = c.editor.frozen_lines().to_vec();` is an unconditional deep copy. frozen_lines() (editor.rs:352-354) returns `&[(usize,usize)]`, so .to_vec() heap-allocates and memcpys every range each call. It IS the odd one out: the adjacent tool_calls_snap/expanded_snap are gen-gated O(1) Rc clones (agent.rs:106-123, only deep-clone when snap_gen advances), and lines_snap is an Rc clone (screens.rs:981). render_agent runs on the root render path (chrome.rs:309/684), and since cx.notify() dirties the only GPUI entity (the root) on chatbox keystrokes — the prompt's stated known-open item — this runs every keystroke, unguarded. The trigger claim is correct.\n\nWhy impact is low, not medium/high: the corrected cost class is benign. The vec holds plain Copy (usize,usize) tuples — no nested allocations, no String clones — so it is a single ~16*N-byte allocation. add_frozen_lines (editor.rs:386-402) merges contiguous/overlapping ranges, so N is the number of disjoint frozen blocks (~one per Claude turn, kept disjoint by interleaved user turns). Even for a long session N is tens-to-low-hundreds, i.e. a few KB and a sub-microsecond alloc per frame. Relative to the genuine per-keystroke cost the prompt already flags (whole-root re-layout because the transcript subtree is not a cached child entity), this is a negligible constant. The recommended Rc-snapshot gen-gate is correct and cheap and worth doing for notify-hygiene parity, but on its own it is a tiny win, not a user-perceptible one.
